## Load Data

```{r}
#| echo: true

## Libraries:
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

## Load data:
## Path to folder...
sox <- read.csv("../data/sockeye/SRDATA2026 1.csv")
stock <- read.csv("../data/sockeye/FC_StockInfo 2.csv")
sox <- sox %>% left_join(stock, by = "PopID")
sox <- sox %>% filter(!is.na(spawners), !is.na(recruits))
```


## Write Likelihood

Equation is:
  
$$
\begin{align}
  log(R_i/S_i) & \sim N(\mu_i, \sigma)\\
  \mu_i & = X_i \cdot \boldsymbol{\beta}.
\end{align}
$$

```{r}
#| echo: true

negloglik <- function(pars){
  beta <- pars[1:npars]
  sigma <- exp(pars[npars+1])
  mu <- X %*% beta
  -sum(dnorm(y, mu, sigma, log = TRUE))
}

## Design Matrix:
X <- model.matrix(log(recruits/spawners) ~ 0 + PopName + PopName:spawners, 
  data = sox)
## Response Variable:
fr <- model.frame(log(recruits/spawners) ~ 0 + PopName + PopName:spawners, 
  data = sox)
y <- model.response(fr)

npars <- ncol(X)
n <- nrow(X)
  
fit <- nlminb(numeric(npars+1), negloglik)
beta_fit <- fit$par[1:npars]
fit_lm <- lm(log(recruits/spawners) ~ 0 + PopName + PopName:spawners, 
  data = sox)
range(beta_fit - coef(fit_lm))
```

Difference can't be explained simply by numerical precision. If we start at the values from `lm` the function stays approximately there.

```{r}
fit_again <- nlminb(c(coef(fit_lm), sigma(fit_lm)/n*(n-npars)), negloglik)
range(fit_again$par[1:npars] - coef(fit_lm))
exp(fit_again$par[npars+1])*sqrt(n/(n-npars)) - sigma(fit_lm)
```

What was wrong with the first fit? 
```{r}
fit
# fit_again
```

What is the gradient there?

```{r}
range(numDeriv::jacobian(negloglik, fit$par))
range(numDeriv::jacobian(negloglik, fit_again$par))
```

Another thing that can be happening is that the values of carrying capacity must be positive. We can inflict that constraint on the model and see if we fit better.

```{r}
which_car <- grep("spawner", colnames(X))
negloglik_2 <- function(pars){
  beta <- pars[1:npars]
  beta[which_car] <- -exp(pars[which_car])
  sigma <- exp(pars[npars+1])
  mu <- X %*% beta
  -sum(dnorm(y, mu, sigma, log = TRUE))
}

fit <- nlminb(numeric(npars+1), negloglik_2)
beta_fit <- fit$par[1:npars]
beta_fit[which_car] <- -exp(beta_fit[which_car])
range(beta_fit - coef(fit_lm))  ## An improvement!
```

## Things to worry about

1. Are the starting values reasonable?
1. What are the constraints on the variables?
1. Are the values I'm fitting very 'small' or very 'large'?

```{r}
library(optimx)
fit_all <- optimx(numeric(npars+1), negloglik, hessian=TRUE,control=list(all.methods=TRUE))
fit_all[!is.na(fit_all$fevals), c("convcode", "fevals", "gevals", "kkt1", "niter", "p31", "value", "xtime")]
```

To start let's just scale the spawners by their standard deviation.

```{r}
sox <- sox %>% 
  mutate(logRS = log(recruits/spawners)) %>% 
  group_by(PopName) %>% 
  mutate(sd_spawners = sd(spawners)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(spawners_scaled = spawners/sd_spawners)

X <- model.matrix(log(recruits/spawners) ~ 0 + PopName + PopName:spawners_scaled, 
  data = sox)

fit_s <- nlminb(numeric(npars+1), negloglik)
scale_back <- sox %>% 
  distinct(PopName, sd_spawners) %>% 
  arrange(PopName)

beta_fit <- fit_s$par[1:npars]
beta_fit[which_car] <- beta_fit[which_car]/scale_back$sd_spawners
range(beta_fit - coef(fit_lm))  ## Getting close!

fit_s$objective + logLik(fit_lm)
```

## A Clean Solution

```{r}
## Nested function for local environment
my_lm <- function(formula, data){
  ## Design Matrix:
  X <- model.matrix(formula, data)
  ## Response Variable:
  fr <- model.frame(formula, data = data)
  y <- model.response(fr)

  npars <- ncol(X)
  pars_init <- numeric(npars+1)
  pars_init[npars+1] <- log(sd(y))
  n <- nrow(X)
  
  ## Nested negative log-likelihood
  ## Parent environment accessible to function this way.
  nll <- function(pars){
    beta <- pars[1:npars]
    sigma <- exp(pars[npars+1])
    mu <- X %*% beta
    -sum(dnorm(y, mu, sigma, log = TRUE))
  }

  fit <- nlminb(pars_init, nll)
  par_values <- fit$par
  beta_fit <- par_values[1:npars]
  names(beta_fit) <- colnames(X)

  if(fit$convergence != 0) cat(" [Warning]", fit$message, ".\n")
  
  return(list(
    beta = beta_fit, 
    sigma = sqrt(n/(n-npars))*exp(par_values[npars+1]), 
    loglik = -fit$obj)
  )
}

fit <- my_lm(log(recruits/spawners) ~ 0 + PopName + PopName:spawners_scaled, 
  data = sox)
```
